options.text: Warming the water tends to reduce how much oxygen stays dissolved in it.
Cold aquarium water can hold more dissolved oxygen than the same water after it is warmed.
Warming the aquarium water increases how much oxygen stays dissolved in it.
Dissolved oxygen stays the same because the water still looks clear.

stem:
Leela keeps fish in a home aquarium. She gently warms the aquarium water with a small heater. She does not bubble extra air into the tank herself.

Which claims correctly predict what happens to dissolved oxygen? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: Gas solubility in water generally falls as temperature rises, so warm water holds less dissolved oxygen than cold water. Clear look does not measure dissolved oxygen.
